dataset: _how to open
description: These files are UTF-8, comma-separated, with a POINT as the decimal separator and ISO dates (YYYY-MM-DD). In Excel do not double-click them: use Data > From Text/CSV, set File Origin to 65001: Unicode (UTF-8), Delimiter to Comma and Locale to English (United States), then Load. Double-clicking on a Dutch Windows uses a semicolon and a decimal comma, which puts every row in one column and turns 1.5 into 15. In Power BI use Get Data > Text/CSV with the same three settings; it will detect them correctly on its own in most cases.

dataset: D3a home delivery, the promise
description: IMPORTANT. This file covers ONE delivery region, not the country. The value is that region's share of national online orders. National order level is over 650,000 rows, which is not a teaching file, so the order-level detail is regional and the national picture lives in home_delivery_daily.csv. Do not scale this file up by dividing: the region is a real region, not a random sample, so its site mix and slot mix are its own. Use it for anything per-order and use the daily file for anything per-chain.
